title: Common flat-tower refinement of a homotopy morphism
statement: Let Y be a scheme, let H be the homotopy category of cochain complexes of its module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let Ctel be the flat-telescope shift representatives [def-sc-flat-telescope-stage-map]. For X,Xprime in Ctel and any s:X→Xprime there exist R in Ctel and a:R→X, b:R→Xprime such that a is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], both a and b are stage-induced maps [def-sc-flat-telescope-stage-map], and a;s=b in H. This is a statement solely about tower presentations and refinement; no derived pullback or normalized comparison occurs.

source.place: Parent lem-sc-normalized-flat-telescope-comparison, steps 1–3; Tags 06YS and 06YJ for flat models. The explicit stage-map refinement and supplied-tensorator normalization are agent expansions, not literal Stacks assertions.

proof.text: Absorb each allowed translate into a telescope presentation. Shift the tower termwise; the shift functor preserves sums and the mapping-cone shift isomorphism identifies its telescope with the shifted original. Boundedness and flatness are preserved degreewise. Transport the given homotopy morphism through the resulting isomorphisms, and lift it to a cochain morphism by fullness of the quotient functor.

Apply the compatible arrow-diagram construction to the cochain arrow. It supplies a common bounded-flat tower, strict sum squares to two target telescope presentations, target homotopy isomorphisms, and an augmentation g to the original source whose stage augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms to its good truncations. Its two cone restrictions and the arrow equality are part of this construction.

The flat truncation telescope comparison applied to q and the two restrictions of g proves g is a quasi-isomorphism. The quotient carries it to a homotopy quasi-isomorphism; composing with the original source isomorphism preserves this property. The common source is a telescope representative by its explicit tower. Each strict sum square gives a stage-map witness with k=0; shift-zero naturality and the composite target isomorphisms give the required transported maps. Postcompose the arrow equality with the original target isomorphism and cancel its inverse to obtain a;s=b.

proof_origin.place: Compatible flat arrow-diagram construction followed by the existing telescope comparison; shift transport and stage-map witnesses are proved directly from Mathlib APIs.
